grid_note: Companion to the WORLD PRESS operator-twin ensemble. Every entry below MUST be forageable by another AI agent tasked with retrieving real archival media (images, videos, patent scans, technical specifications) for use as ground-truth stand-ins in place of the BEFLIX renders. For counterfactual and speculative loci the forage MUST NOT fabricate primary sources; it MUST gather the closest-adjacent real material and label it 'analogue' with the analogue relationship explicit.

source_status_definitions.documented: The event occurred as described. Primary sources (patents, papers, photographs, films, press) exist and MUST be located.
source_status_definitions.inferred: The event is a bridge between documented events (e.g. the 'VR Winter'). Named era exists in retrospect; forage retrospective analysis + press coverage of its dates.
source_status_definitions.speculative: The event is a plausible near-future extrapolation not yet realized. Forage the closest real analogue (standards drafts, open protocols, precedents) and label as analogue.
source_status_definitions.counterfactual: The event never occurred. Forage the closest real analogue and label as analogue. NEVER present analogue material as primary evidence of the counterfactual event.

theme_axes.sensory: How much of the sensorium the milestone engages (LOW = eyes only; HIGH = eyes + ears + touch + smell + wind).
theme_axes.interaction: How much bidirectional coupling with the human body (LOW = passive viewing; HIGH = gestural / haptic / voice).
theme_axes.institutional: How much sponsorship by an institution (LOW = individual / consumer; HIGH = state / military / academy).
theme_axes.scale: How many people are addressed (LOW = one seat; HIGH = mass consumer market).

media_target_schema.primary_docs: Patents, papers, technical reports, standards documents. Highest fidelity.
media_target_schema.photographs: Contemporaneous still photographs of the apparatus, ideally from the inventor/institution.
media_target_schema.film_or_video: Contemporaneous moving image of the apparatus in use, or a modern demonstration of a surviving unit.
media_target_schema.press: Contemporaneous magazine / newspaper coverage (Time, Scientific American, Wired).
media_target_schema.artifacts: Museum holdings — accession numbers, on-display locations.

3d-golden.title: 3D FILM GOLDEN ERA
3d-golden.one_line: The audience wearing paper glasses learns the screen can reach outward.
3d-golden.why_it_matters: First mass-market immersion of the twentieth century; establishes the paying single-seat body as the target of the medium.
artifacts_of_interest: Original Bwana Devil / House of Wax lobby cards

photographs: audiences wearing paper glasses in 1952 theaters (Life magazine spreads)
film_or_video: House of Wax (1953) trailer public archive
diagrams: Natural Vision dual-camera and dual-projector rig

3d-golden.forage_instruction: Find contemporaneous audience photographs, at least one surviving trailer, and one press spread showing the paper-glasses ritual. Prefer public-domain reproductions.

telesphere.title: HEILIG TELESPHERE MASK
telesphere.one_line: Heilig straps the cinema directly onto a single human face.
telesphere.why_it_matters: First patented head-mounted display; the cinema apparatus becomes wearable.

primary_docs: US 2,955,156 full PDF including all figures
diagrams: Patent Figs 1-6: mask cross-section, optics, strap
photographs: Heilig with Telesphere prototype, held by HMH Foundation Moving Image Archive

telesphere.forage_instruction: Retrieve the full patent PDF (all 6 figures) and the HMH Foundation photographs. The patent figures are the highest-fidelity available representation.

sensorama.title: SENSORAMA
sensorama.one_line: A cabinet that touched every sense at once, and asked nothing back.
sensorama.why_it_matters: First multisensory (sight/sound/wind/smell/vibration) single-viewer simulator; the direct ancestor of every 'immersive experience' apparatus that follows.

essay.title: The Cinema of the Future
essay.author: Morton L. Heilig
essay.note: Heilig's own theoretical statement; predates the Sensorama patent.

artifacts_of_interest: Surviving Sensorama unit (Ivan Sutherland collection / HMH Foundation)

film_or_video: Rheingold 1991 description of trying the Brooklyn ride reel

sensorama.forage_instruction: Retrieve US 3,050,870 (all 8 sheets), any surviving stills of the five short films, and the Industrial Design 1964 spread. This milestone has the richest primary-source trail; forage should aim for maximum fidelity.

ultimate-display.title: THE ULTIMATE DISPLAY
ultimate-display.one_line: Sutherland names the endpoint: a room that is itself the display.
ultimate-display.why_it_matters: The theoretical horizon of the field, written in one paragraph in 1965 and quoted every decade since.
ultimate-display.forage_instruction: This is a TEXT milestone (a paper, not an apparatus). Retrieve the complete paper PDF. Visual output should be the paper's scanned pages themselves; do not force imagery where none exists.

damocles.title: SWORD OF DAMOCLES
damocles.one_line: The first head-mounted 3-D display; ceiling-suspended because it is too heavy for a neck.
damocles.why_it_matters: First real-time perspective-correct stereoscopic head-tracked display; the ceiling arm becomes the field's founding image.

paper.title: A Head-Mounted Three-Dimensional Display
paper.author: Ivan E. Sutherland
paper.venue: AFIPS Fall Joint Computer Conference Proceedings

artifacts_of_interest: Original Sword of Damocles apparatus (Computer History Museum, Mountain View — CHM Revolution collection)

photographs: Sutherland-era Lincoln Lab photograph of user under ceiling arm
artifacts: CHM Revolution entry: 'The Sword of Damocles: Early head-mounted display'

damocles.naming_caveat: Sutherland himself has said 'Sword of Damocles' referred only to the mechanical head-tracking arm; the display was called 'the head-mounted display'. Foragers must preserve this distinction.
damocles.forage_instruction: Retrieve the AFIPS paper, the CHM artifact photographs, and at least one contemporaneous photograph of a user in the apparatus. Include the naming caveat in the metadata for any downstream visualization.

public-grid.title: PUBLIC SENSORIUM GRID
public-grid.one_line: The sensorium built as civic infrastructure rather than as a single-seat cabinet.
public-grid.counterfactual_hypothesis: If Heilig's Experience Theater patent (US 3,469,837, 1969) had been treated as public infrastructure rather than an unfunded proposal, the 1970s would have delivered municipal sensorium halls.

adjacent_real_precedents.name: Heilig Experience Theater patent
adjacent_real_precedents.note: Heilig's own scaled-up multi-viewer version of the Sensorama; never built.

adjacent_real_precedents.name: Cinerama and Circle-Vision 360
adjacent_real_precedents.note: The closest real municipal-scale immersive cinema of the era.

adjacent_real_precedents.name: Expo '67 and Expo '70 pavilions
adjacent_real_precedents.note: State-funded immersive spectacle at civic scale.

primary_docs: US 3,469,837 (Experience Theater) — Heilig's own scaled-up proposal

public-grid.forage_instruction: DO NOT fabricate 'photographs of the Public Sensorium Grid.' Retrieve US 3,469,837 as the closest primary source (it is Heilig's own proposal for exactly this) and Cinerama / Expo '67 / Expo '70 pavilion imagery as analogues. Label every asset with analogue_relationship: 'nearest real precedent'.

nasa-view.title: NASA VIEW PROGRAM
nasa-view.one_line: The state funds telepresence; immersion becomes an instrument of agencies.
nasa-view.why_it_matters: First institutionally-scaled VR lab; introduces the head-mounted display + dataglove + 3D-audio triad that the consumer industry inherits.

paper_1986.title: Virtual Environment Display System
paper_1986.venue: ACM 1986 Workshop on Interactive 3D Graphics, Chapel Hill NC

archive_finding_aid.title: Guide to the Human Systems Integration Division Virtual Environment Documentation and Equipment, 1987-1993

artifacts_of_interest: NASA VIEW prototype 3 headset — on display at Smithsonian Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center, Chantilly VA
VIEWlab fiberoptic dataglove prototype, 1987, NASA Ames

photographs: VIEWlab System Prototype 3 (1988) — subject wearing motorcycle-helmet HMD
simulation: NASA VIEWlab VR Experience (Immersive Archive, in development)

nasa-view.forage_instruction: Retrieve the finding aid PDF (it enumerates every VIEW photograph and film in the archive), the two Fisher papers, and the Robinett site's photographs. This milestone has the deepest institutional archive of any documented milestone.

vpl.title: VPL RESEARCH — DATAGLOVE + EYEPHONE
institutions: VPL Research (Palo Alto / Redwood City CA)
vpl.one_line: Two gloved hands meet in a shared synthetic room; the term 'virtual reality' enters the language.
vpl.why_it_matters: First commercial VR products; coining and popularization of the term itself.

scientific_american_cover.note: First mass-audience cover treatment of gestural VR.

artifacts_of_interest: VPL DataGlove (Computer History Museum, MIT Museum)

photographs: June 7 1989 Texpo Telecommunications Show demonstration (two people with EyePhones + DataGloves)
film_or_video: 1990s Kinolibrary archive footage of Lanier demonstrating VPL DataGlove
The Lawnmower Man (1992) — DataSuit + EyePhone as fiction

vpl.forage_instruction: Prefer the June 1989 Texpo demonstration photograph as the canonical still. Retrieve the Kinolibrary Lanier demo clip. The Lawnmower Man is FICTION and must be labeled as cultural reception, not evidence of the apparatus.

arcade-era.title: VR ARCADE DOMINANCE
arcade-era.one_line: Immersion stays social, coin-fed, and loud, cabinet by cabinet.
arcade-era.counterfactual_hypothesis: Virtuality Group and their imitators sustained a mass social arcade format instead of collapsing into VR winter.

adjacent_real_precedents.name: Virtuality 1000CS / 1000SD
adjacent_real_precedents.note: Real arcade VR cabinets deployed in shopping centers 1991-94. Ran Dactyl Nightmare, Legend Quest, etc. Closest real analogue to the counterfactual.

adjacent_real_precedents.name: Sega VR-1
adjacent_real_precedents.note: Six-seat motion simulator at Joypolis and SegaWorld.

photographs: Virtuality 1000CS cabinet in a UK arcade circa 1992-93
film_or_video: Retrospective demonstrations of surviving Virtuality units
artifacts: Virtuality cabinets held by private collectors / retro-VR museums

arcade-era.forage_instruction: This milestone did not occur at scale. Retrieve Virtuality Group and Sega VR-1 material as adjacent analogues. Label all imagery analogue_relationship: 'the real arcade VR that did NOT dominate'. Foragers must not present this as evidence of a sustained era.

vr-winter.title: THE VR WINTER
vr-winter.one_line: The market exhales. Headsets go quiet in storage for a decade.
vr-winter.why_it_matters: The negative space that separates VPL and Oculus; a named era only in retrospect.
canonical_signals: VPL Research bankruptcy (1990); patents to Sun Microsystems (1998/1999)
Absence of new HMD product launches 1996-2011

press: Retrospective analyses (Wired, Ars Technica, Polygon) framing the 1995-2012 gap
photographs: Virtual Boy in retail dump bins
VR headsets in museum storage / retrospective magazine layouts

vr-winter.forage_instruction: This is an ABSENCE — a Sonsign, a sound of nothing. Do NOT fabricate primary sources. Retrieve retrospective press labeling the era, plus Virtual Boy failure documentation as the era's canonical apparatus. The best media may be layouts of empty shelves or Virtual Boy in landfill photography.

oculus.title: OCULUS RIFT KICKSTARTER
oculus.one_line: A crowd funds the revival, one small pledge at a time.
oculus.why_it_matters: Ends the VR winter with a distributed-funding revival; announces the consumer era.

kickstarter.title: Oculus Rift: Step Into the Game

photographs: Palmer Luckey with early Rift prototype

oculus.forage_instruction: The Kickstarter pitch video and page are the canonical primary sources. Retrieve the Internet Archive snapshot in case the page changes.

consumer-vr.title: CONSUMER VR LAUNCH
consumer-vr.one_line: Immersion arrives in living rooms, boxed, tethered, and priced.
consumer-vr.why_it_matters: The first mass-market simultaneous launch of consumer VR — Oculus Rift CV1, HTC Vive, PSVR all in one calendar year.

photographs: Retail box shots of all three headsets
Living-room deployment photographs with tether cables and lighthouse trackers
film_or_video: Manufacturer launch keynotes and TV commercials
press: The Verge, IGN, Polygon 2016 launch reviews

consumer-vr.forage_instruction: Retrieve retail packaging and installation photography rather than 'user in headset' publicity shots; the story is the arrival of the box in the home.

open-standard.title: OPEN EMBODIMENT STANDARD
open-standard.one_line: A protocol, not a product: embodiment becomes a commons.
open-standard.speculative_hypothesis: OpenXR or a successor becomes the dominant embodiment standard, breaking platform lock-in.
open-standard.forage_instruction: Retrieve the OpenXR spec and Khronos diagrams as adjacent real precedents. This milestone SPECULATES a further victory; label material analogue_relationship: 'closest real precedent that could become this milestone'.

vision-pro.title: APPLE VISION PRO
vision-pro.one_line: The room seals. The platform decides what the senses receive.
vision-pro.why_it_matters: The most vertically-integrated consumer immersion product to date; endpoint of the platform-consolidation trajectory.

photographs: Apple's official product photography — the sealed-frame silhouette
press: The Verge, Wired, MKBHD reviews Feb 2024

vision-pro.forage_instruction: Apple's official product photography and the WWDC 2023 keynote are canonical. Retrieve at least one photograph showing the outward-facing display (EyeSight) — this is the visual signature of the enclosure.

world_state_ontology.note: Each sampled world is a complete <World Instance> per the parent theory. This section enumerates the shape of a world's state so a forager can produce the same structure for any counterfactual traversal.

state_fields.chain: ordered milestone ids, always beginning with 3d-golden
state_fields.trace: per-step record: {from, eligible, sample, chosen, prob, forced}

ending_classes.meaning: the sample ended before the field resolved

forage_output_schema.note: Every asset returned by the forager MUST conform to this schema so downstream tools can wire them into the interface as ground-truth stand-ins.

record.milestone_id: must match a key under milestones
record.analogue_relationship: null for documented; one of {'nearest real precedent','the real arcade VR that did NOT dominate','closest real precedent that could become this milestone','retrospective naming of an absence'} for the others
record.title: string
record.creator: string or list
record.archival_repository: institution name and accession id where applicable
record.rights: public domain | CC-BY | fair use (educational) | proprietary — use with permission
record.resolution_or_pages: for images: WxH; for docs: page count
record.local_path: where the forager should write the retrieved file
record.why_chosen: one sentence justifying the asset's canonical status for this milestone
